greek: ᾿Αλλὰ χαὶ ἐὰν φῇς, Δεῖξόν μοι τὸν Θεόν σου χἀγώ σοι εἴποιμι ἂν, Δεῖξόν μοι τὸν ἄνθρωπόν σου, χἀγώ σοι δείξω τὸν Θεόν μου. english: But if you say, Show me your God, I would reply, Show me yourself, and I will show you my God. Show, then, that the eyes of your soul are capable of seeing, and the ears of your heart able to hear; [...] For God is seen by those who are enabled to see Him when they have the eyes of their soul opened
page: page unknown (the PG 6 OCR gives no reliable column for this passage; New Advent and CCEL carry no ANF page numbers)
edition: Migne PG 6 (Paris 1857), Greek; Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885), Dods translation, as on New Advent
what_it_says: God is seen only by those whose soul's eyes are opened (purified); bodily sight cannot see him.
limits: Answers Autolycus's demand to see God; says nothing about Word, Wisdom or Spirit. The 'eyes of the soul' point is ethical (sin darkens the soul), not a doctrine of the Son.

greek: Τὸ μὲν εἶδος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἄῤῥητον χαὶ ἀνέχφραστον χαὶ μὴ δυνάμενον ὁφθαλμοῖς σαρχίνοις ὁραθῆναι. Δόξῃ γάρ ἐστιν ἀχώρητος, μεγέθει ἀχατάληπτος, ὕψει ἀπερινόητος, ἐσχύ" ἀπύγχριτος, σοφίᾳ ἀσυμόίδαστος, ἀγαθοσύνῃ ἀμίμητος, χαλοποιΐᾳ ἀνεχδιήγητος. english: The appearance of God is ineffable and indescribable, and cannot be seen by eyes of flesh. For in glory He is incomprehensible, in greatness unfathomable, in height inconceivable, in power incomparable, in wisdom unrivalled, in goodness inimitable, in kindness unutterable. For if I say He is Light, I name but His own work; if I call Him Word, I name but His sovereignty;
page: page unknown (the PG 6 OCR gives no reliable column for this passage; New Advent and CCEL carry no ANF page numbers)
edition: Migne PG 6 (Paris 1857), Greek; Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885), Dods translation, as on New Advent
what_it_says: God is ineffable; each name for God (Light, Word, Mind, Spirit, Wisdom and others) names only one of his works or attributes; 'Word' names God's sovereignty.
limits: The Word is listed among about a dozen equal-status 'names' of God, all said to name his works or attributes; it is not presented as a distinct person. Dods renders archen (ἀρχήν) as 'sovereignty'; the Greek word also means 'beginning' (Book 2 'arche' passages were not read here).

what_it_says: 'Spirit' is God's breath and 'Wisdom' is his offspring, both listed as ways of speaking about God.
limits: Spirit is 'breath' (anapnoe, ἀναπνοή), an impersonal reading; Wisdom is 'offspring' (gennema, γέννημα), generation language relevant to the generation debate. No Holy Spirit as a person is named here. Greek 'krata' (κράτος) is rendered 'sway'.

english: And He is without beginning, because He is unbegotten; and He is unchangeable, because He is immortal. And he is called God [Θεός] on account of His having placed [τεθεικέναι] all things on security afforded by Himself; and on account of [θέειν], for θέειν means running, and moving, and being active, and nourishing, and foreseeing, and governing, and making all things alive. But he is Lord, because He rules over the universe; Father, because he is before all things;
page: page unknown (the PG 6 OCR gives no reliable column for this passage; New Advent and CCEL carry no ANF page numbers)

what_it_says: God is 'unbegotten' (agennetos) and so without beginning, and 'Father' because he is before all things.
limits: The attribute 'unbegotten' is said of God as such, and the Word or Son is not mentioned in this chapter. Relevant to any claim that only the Father is unbegotten, since the Word or Son is not mentioned in this chapter. Greek ἤΆναρχος opens with an OCR-garbled letter.

Ὥσπερ οὖν ὁ κόχχος τῆς ῥοᾶς ἔνδον χατοιχῶν οὐ δύναται ὁρᾷν τὰ ἔξω τοῦ λέπους αὐτὸς ὧν ἔνδον οὕτως οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπος ἐμπεριεχόμενος μετὰ πάσης τῆς χτίσεως ὑπὸ χειρὸς Θεοῦ οὐ δύναται θεωρεῖν τὸν Θεόν.

english: For as the pomegranate, with the rind containing it, has within it many cells and compartments which are separated by tissues, and has also many seeds dwelling in it, so the whole creation is contained by the spirit of God, and the containing spirit is along with the creation contained by the hand of God. As, therefore, the seed of the pomegranate, dwelling inside, cannot see what is outside the rind, itself being within; so neither can man, who along with the whole creation is enclosed by the hand of God, behold God.
page: page unknown (the PG 6 OCR gives no reliable column for this passage; New Advent and CCEL carry no ANF page numbers)
edition: Migne PG 6 (Paris 1857), Greek; Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885), Dods translation, as on New Advent
what_it_says: The whole creation is held in the 'containing spirit' of God, which is itself held by God's hand; man cannot see God from inside creation.
limits: The 'spirit' (pneuma) here is a cosmic, Stoic-style environing spirit that sustains creation, not a Holy Spirit person. The passage does not distinguish persons.

english: Who is the Physician? God, who heals and makes alive through His word and wisdom. God by His own word and wisdom made all things;
page: page unknown (the PG 6 OCR gives no reliable column for this passage; New Advent and CCEL carry no ANF page numbers)

what_it_says: God heals and makes alive 'through' his Word and his Wisdom, and made all things through them.

english: God by His own word and wisdom made all things; for by His word were the heavens made, and all the host of them by the breath of His mouth. Most excellent is His wisdom. By His wisdom God founded the earth; and by knowledge he prepared the heavens; and by understanding were the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the clouds poured out their dews.
page: page unknown (the PG 6 OCR gives no reliable column for this passage; New Advent and CCEL carry no ANF page numbers)
edition: Migne PG 6 (Paris 1857), Greek; Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885), Dods translation, as on New Advent
what_it_says: Creation is made through God's Word, his Wisdom and his Spirit (pneuma): the heavens by the Word, the host of heaven by the Spirit, and the earth by Wisdom.
limits: The three agents appear together in one creation formula, the nearest thing in Book I to a triad, but the word 'Triad' does not occur here (it is in 2.15). Dods renders pneuma as 'breath of His mouth' ('of His mouth' is Dods's addition; Ps 33:6 is the likely source). Dods renders phronesei as 'by knowledge' and aisthesei as 'by understanding'. Greek 'Ἱκρατίστη' is OCR-garbled.

english: I met with the sacred Scriptures of the holy prophets, who also by the Spirit of God foretold the things that have already happened, just as they came to pass, and the things now occurring as they are now happening, and things future in the order in which they shall be accomplished.

what_it_says: The holy prophets spoke by the Spirit of God, foretelling past, present and future events.
limits: 'Spirit of God' as the source of prophecy is ordinary Christian language, but the Greek has no 'holy' (hagion) with 'pneuma' in Book I (checked). It does not say the Spirit is a person. Greek 'ἐνε«τῶτα τίν:' is OCR-garbled.

english: for if you do this, you do the will of God. For the law that is of God, says, My son, fear the Lord and the king, and be not disobedient to them; for suddenly they shall take vengeance on their enemies.

what_it_says: A quotation of the law ('My son, honour God and the king') addressed to a human reader; it is the only vocative 'son' (υἱέ) in Book I.
limits: This is the negative item: Book I has no 'Son of God' (υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ) for Christ. Dods's 'fear the Lord' does not match the Greek 'Τίμα' (honour); the Greek says 'God' and 'king' (Θεὸν καὶ βασιλέα). The OCR heading '14..' does not match Dods's chapter 11; the chapter is identified by content.

english: and, since, besides, you call me a Christian, as if this were a damning name to bear, I, for my part, avow that I am a Christian, and bear this name beloved of God, hoping to be serviceable to God.

limits: Responds to Autolycus's mockery of the name; no doctrinal content about the Word, Wisdom or Spirit.
